description: Check the current health status for one or more vendors. Accepts registered vendor slugs (e.g., "github", "aws", "gcp", "gitlab") or raw Atlassian Statuspage base URLs. Registry entries are served by each vendor's native status API (Statuspage, Status.io, Slack, AWS Health, Google Cloud Service Health, Azure status, Azure DevOps status, Firehydrant) and normalized to one shape. Returns per-vendor operational indicator as the vendor published it (none = no degradation reported, minor, major, critical, maintenance = scheduled window), degraded components, and active incidents; summary counts each vendor at the worse of its indicator and its worst open incident rated minor or worse. Use mode: "detailed" for component lists and maintenance windows, narrowed with component_filter, bounded by component_limit, and paged with component_offset. Batch-friendly — pass a list to check your full stack in one call; up to 20 vendors are checked per call, and any past the 20th come back in deferred_vendors to resend. A vendor that cannot be resolved or reached is reported in its own result row, so one bad entry never discards the rest. Every vendor with an active problem gets a pre-filled devops_suggest_action call in nextToolSuggestions.

component_filter.description: Case-insensitive substring matched against component names and their group names in detailed mode (e.g., "api" to check just the API components, or a product or region a page groups components under). Applied before component_offset and component_limit, so it reaches a specific component without paging, and an offset pages within the filtered list. A filter that matches nothing for a vendor is reported in notice. Ignored in summary mode.

component_limit.description: Maximum components returned per vendor in detailed mode, at least 1. A value above 500 is reduced to 500, and notice says so; a longer list continues with component_offset. Large status pages publish hundreds of components, so a multi-vendor batch at a high limit returns a very large response; narrow with component_filter instead where possible.

component_offset.description: Components to skip per vendor, after component_filter and before component_limit. Pass a vendor's next_component_offset to continue its list. An offset past a vendor's last component returns an empty list for it, and notice says so. Ignored in summary mode.

mode.description: summary: indicator + degraded components + active incidents only. detailed: adds the component list and scheduled maintenance windows.

vendors.description: Vendor slugs from the built-in registry (e.g., "github", "aws") or raw Atlassian Statuspage base URLs (non-Statuspage backends are supported via registry slugs only). Mix freely. Use devops_list_vendors to discover available slugs. The first 20 are checked, in the order given; entries past the 20th are returned unchecked in deferred_vendors to resend in another call. Lists longer than 100 are rejected.

items.description: A vendor slug (e.g., "github") or raw Atlassian Statuspage base URL.

name: devops_status_check

cap.description: The per-vendor component_limit that was applied. Present only when truncated.

deferred_vendors.description: Entries past the first 20 in vendors, verbatim and in input order. They were not checked; resend them in another call. Empty when every entry was checked.

items.description: A vendor entry exactly as provided.

error.description: Present when the call failed. Absent on success.

code.description: JSON-RPC error code for this failure.

reason.description: Machine-readable failure mode. Declared by this tool: `vendor_not_found`: No requested vendor among the first 20 could be checked and the first failure was a slug that matches no registry entry and is not a valid URL. `target_blocked`: No requested vendor among the first 20 could be checked and the first failure was a raw URL resolving to a private, loopback, or cloud-metadata address. Other values are possible when a failure originates below the handler.

recovery.description: Actionable next step for the caller.

message.description: Human-readable description of what went wrong.

nextToolSuggestions.description: One devops_suggest_action call per vendor with an active problem — an indicator of minor, major, or critical, or an open incident of that impact even while the indicator reads none or maintenance; these are the vendors summary counts as degraded or down — with its arguments filled from that vendor's result. Vendors that could not be checked never appear. Empty when no checked vendor has an active problem.

items.description: A recommended follow-up tool call with pre-filled arguments.

args.description: Ready-to-use devops_suggest_action arguments: vendor (registry slug, or the normalized status page URL for a raw URL), vendor_indicator (only for minor, major, or critical), affected_components (degraded components outside a maintenance window, each written "Group / Leaf" when it is in a group), incident_summary (title of the most recently started open incident rated minor or worse).

reason.description: Why the vendor qualifies: its reported indicator, or the open incident behind it.

notice.description: Plain-language explanation of what this call left out or adjusted, in this order: vendors past the first 20 (listed in deferred_vendors); a component_limit above 500 reduced to 500; in detailed mode, how many components lie past the returned page and how to reach them (this tool again with that vendor and its next_component_offset as component_offset, component_filter to target one, or component_limit to raise a cap below 500), which vendors component_offset ran past the end of, and which checked vendors component_filter matched no component of, with how many each publishes; and last, for a vendor whose entry reads an umbrella status page with no components (atlassian), the slugs of the entries reading its product pages. Present only when one of these applies.

results.description: Per-vendor status results for the vendors checked, in the same order as the input vendors list.

items.description: Status result for a single vendor.

id.description: Unique incident identifier from the vendor's status API.

impact.description: Severity level: none = informational, minor = degraded performance, major = partial outage, critical = full outage, maintenance = scheduled window folded into incident history.

latest_update.description: Most recent update text, as plain text: HTML markup the vendor published is converted, and any other < is text the vendor wrote.

started_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp, with the vendor's UTC offset (Z, +00:00, or a local offset such as -07:00), when the incident started, or null/absent if not set by the vendor.

status.description: Current incident status (e.g., investigating, monitoring, resolved).

all_components.description: Components including operational ones, narrowed by component_filter (matched against name and group) when given, starting at component_offset (devops_status_check only; the first component otherwise), and at most component_limit per vendor. Present in detailed mode only.

description.description: Component description, or null if not provided.

group.description: Name of the group the status page files this component under — typically the product or region it belongs to — or null when it is not in a group.

name.description: Component name as the status page publishes it — the leaf alone, without its group. Several leaves can share a name (one per region or product); group tells them apart.

all_components_total.description: Components matching component_filter for this vendor, before component_offset and component_limit — the length of the whole list all_components is a page of. Present in detailed mode only.

cached.description: True when this result was served from the in-memory status cache, shared across callers (60 s TTL by default), so its data can be up to that TTL older than checked_at.

checked_at.description: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp of this check — when this result was built, not when the status data was fetched; see cached.

degraded_components.description: Every component not in an operational state, uncapped — a vendor with a large edge-node fleet routinely publishes dozens. Includes in-progress maintenance windows (status under_maintenance) alongside genuine outages; read status to tell a planned window from a fault. Empty when all clear.

group.description: Name of the group the status page files this component under — typically the product or region it belongs to — or null when it is not in a group.

name.description: Component name as the status page publishes it — the leaf alone, without its group. Several leaves can share a name (one per region or product); group tells them apart.

status.description: Degradation level: degraded_performance = slow/intermittent, partial_outage = some requests failing, major_outage = most requests failing, under_maintenance = scheduled maintenance in progress.

error.description: Why this vendor could not be checked — unreachable status API, timeout, non-2xx, or a response that is not a Statuspage payload. Reported here rather than thrown so one bad vendor does not fail the batch. Absent when the vendor was fetched successfully.

indicator.description: Overall health indicator, as the vendor published it: none = no degradation reported, minor = some degradation, major = significant outage, critical = complete outage, maintenance = scheduled window in progress, planned rather than a fault. A page can rate it from component statuses alone, so it can read none or maintenance while active_incidents lists an open incident rated minor or worse; summary, and devops_watch_stack's health, rate the vendor by the worse of the two.

next_component_offset.description: Where this vendor's component list continues. Present in detailed mode only, and only when components remain past the returned page: pass it as component_offset to devops_status_check, with this vendor, mode "detailed", and the same component_filter. Absent on the last page.

scheduled_maintenances.description: Upcoming or in-progress maintenance windows. Present in detailed mode only.

scheduled_for.description: ISO 8601 start time, with the vendor's UTC offset.

scheduled_until.description: ISO 8601 end time, with the vendor's UTC offset, or null when the vendor's feed publishes no planned end.

statuspage_url.description: Status page base URL used for this vendor.

vendor.description: Vendor slug or URL as provided.

shown.description: Components returned across all vendors. Present only when truncated.

summary.description: Aggregate health counts across all checked vendors. Each vendor is rated by the worse of its indicator and its worst open incident rated minor or worse; an incident rated none or maintenance never raises the rating. Buckets partition the batch: operational + degraded + down + maintenance + unavailable = total.

maintenance.description: Vendors rated maintenance — in a scheduled window the vendor published, with no open incident rated minor or worse. Counted apart from degraded and down, which are faults.

operational.description: Vendors rated none — indicator none and no open incident rated minor or worse — and not errored.

total.description: Total number of vendors checked — never counts deferred_vendors.

unavailable.description: Vendors that could not be checked (carry an error) — unresolvable slug, blocked target, or failed status fetch. Counted as unknown, never operational.

totalCount.description: Components matching component_filter across all vendors, before component_offset and the cap. Present only when truncated.

truncated.description: True when at least one vendor has components past the returned page — those vendors carry next_component_offset. Absent otherwise, including on the last page of a list.

title: Devops Status Check
